title: London to LA: what's underneath?
hook: On a wall map, London to LA looks like a hop over the Atlantic. Fly it and look down.

knows: that long flights look curved on flat maps
roughly where Greenland, Iceland and Canada are
doesNotKnow: how to see the shortest path as a straight line
what the London to Los Angeles shortest path passes over

misconception: A flight from London to Los Angeles crosses open Atlantic and then Canada, because the straight line on a Mercator map does.
objective: The learner can explain that on a gnomonic map every great circle is straight, that the shortest London to Los Angeles route crosses the southern tip of Greenland, and that the straight line on Mercator is a longer constant-bearing route.

claims.text: On a gnomonic map every great circle, the shortest path between two points on a ball, is a straight line.
claims.source: Snyder (1987), Map Projections: A Working Manual, USGS PP 1395, ch. 22 (Gnomonic). From memory, not checked online. d3-geo geoGnomonic.

claims.text: A gnomonic map shows less than half the globe.
claims.source: Points 90° from the centre project to infinity (r = R tan c). The lesson clips at 52° from the route's midpoint.

claims.text: The shortest London to Los Angeles route crosses the southern tip of Greenland, not Iceland or only open ocean.
claims.source: geoInterpolate between London (51.5072°N, 0.1276°W) and Los Angeles (34.0522°N, 118.2437°W), sampled at 2,000 points against the kit's 1:110m countries with geoContains: UK, Ireland, sea, Greenland (about 2,780-3,156 km out, 42.6°W-49.9°W at about 62.3°N), sea, Canada, United States. Iceland's outline is about 432 km from the route at its closest. City coordinates from memory, not checked online. The 1:110m outline is coarse; the lesson says 'southern tip' and gives no length for the land leg (brief rule 4). The stage's marker shows 'Greenland' at the 3,000 km slider stop.

claims.text: The shortest London to Los Angeles route is about 8,760 km on a round Earth, ignoring winds.
claims.source: d3-geo geoDistance x 6,371.0088 km = 8,755.6 km (shown to the nearest 10 km). Sphere model. No claim that any airline flies this exact path; real routes vary with winds and airspace.

claims.text: The line that looks straight on Mercator is a constant compass bearing; from London to Los Angeles it crosses open Atlantic far south of Greenland and is about 9,730 km, longer than the shortest route.
claims.source: Rhumb-line length d = sqrt(Δφ² + q² Δλ²) R with q = Δφ / Δψ, Δψ = ln(tan(π/4 + φ2/2) / tan(π/4 + φ1/2)) (Snyder 1987, ch. 7; from memory). Computed in Demo.tsx rhumbKm: 9,733 km. Mercator rhumb lines are straight: Snyder ch. 7.

recall.question: You want to see the shortest route between two cities as a straight line. Which kind of map do you use?
options: Any map, if you draw carefully
recall.why: Gnomonic maps send every great circle to a straight line. On Mercator a straight line is a constant compass bearing, which is longer.
